M&A interview question

You buy a company for $500M. Where does the extra money go?

Bankers get this one in almost every accounting round.

The question

Price paid: $500M. Fair value of the target's net assets: $350M. Goodwill?

A$500M
B$350M
C$150M
D$850M

Pick one, then swipe.

Answer
C. $150M
$500M
Purchase pricewhat the buyer pays
−$350M
Fair value of net assetsassets minus liabilities
$150M
Goodwillthe premium over fair value

What it really is

Goodwill is the part of the price you can't point to on the balance sheet.

Brand, customers, team, expected synergies. It sits on the buyer's balance sheet as an asset.

Curveball 🔥

The target's assets get marked up $50M to fair value. Goodwill now?

$100M

Fair value of net assets goes to $400M, so the premium shrinks: $500M − $400M.

Bonus point

Public U.S. companies don't amortize goodwill.

It's tested for impairment at least once a year. If the deal goes bad, it gets written down.

Did you get it? 👇
